at pakke.explanation: "At pakke" means "to pack", for example a suitcase or a bag: "Jeg pakker min kuffert" (I pack my suitcase). It also means "to wrap": "pakke en gave ind" (to wrap a present). "En pakke" (a parcel) looks the same.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **pakke** min kuffert, for vi rejser i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to pack my suitcase, because we are travelling tomorrow.

at prøve.explanation: "At prøve" means "to try": "Jeg prøver at lære dansk" (I am trying to learn Danish). It also means "to try on", for example "prøve en kjole" (to try on a dress). "En prøve" means "a test" or "a sample".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **prøve** at lære dansk, selv om det er svært.
sentence.en: I want to try to learn Danish, even though it is hard.

at prøve tøj.explanation: "At prøve tøj" means "to try on clothes", for example in a shop. To ask about one item, you can say "Må jeg prøve den?" (May I try it on?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **prøve tøj** i butikken.
sentence.en: I would like to try on clothes in the shop.

en pakke.explanation: "En pakke" means "a package" or "a parcel", and also "a packet", like "en pakke smør" (a packet of butter). You can say "Der er kommet en pakke" (A parcel has arrived). "At pakke" means "to pack".

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **pakke** med posten i dag.
sentence.en: I got a package in the mail today.

en pandekage.explanation: "En pandekage" means "a pancake", built from "pande" (a pan) and "kage" (a cake). A frying pan is "en pande".

sentence.da: Jeg steger en tynd **pandekage** på panden og spiser den med syltetøj.
sentence.en: I fry a thin pancake in the pan and eat it with jam.

en paraply.explanation: "En paraply" means "an umbrella", said pa-ra-PLY, with the stress on the last part. The "y" sounds like a rounded "ee", with the lips pushed forward.

sentence.da: Det regner, så jeg tager en **paraply** med.
sentence.en: It is raining, so I take an umbrella with me.

en park.explanation: "En park" means "a park". You say "i parken" (in the park). Do not mix it up with "at parkere" (to park a car).

sentence.da: Vi går en tur i en stor **park** med træer og blomster.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in a big park with trees and flowers.

en patient.explanation: "En patient" means "a patient", a person getting medical care. It is spelled the same as the English word. Patients are found at "et sygehus" (a hospital) or "en klinik" (a clinic).

sentence.da: Lægen hjælper en syg **patient** på sygehuset.
sentence.en: The doctor helps a sick patient at the hospital.

en pause.explanation: "En pause" means "a break" or "a pause", for example at work or school. "At holde pause" means "to take a break", and "en kaffepause" (a coffee break) is a short one.

sentence.da: Vi har arbejdet længe, så nu holder vi **pause** og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: We have worked a long time, so now we take a break and drink coffee.

en pen.explanation: "En pen" means "a pen". Do not mix it up with "pæn" (nice, pretty), which is spelled with an "æ". A ballpoint pen is "en kuglepen" (a ballpoint pen).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mit navn på papiret med en **pen**.
sentence.en: I write my name on the paper with a pen.

en perron.explanation: "En perron" means "a platform" at a train station. You say "på perronen" (on the platform) and "Toget kører fra perron 3" (The train leaves from platform 3).

sentence.da: Vi står på **perron** to og venter på toget.
sentence.en: We stand on platform two and wait for the train.

en person.explanation: "En person" means "a person". When booking you say "et bord til to personer" (a table for two people). For people in general, Danes often say "mennesker" (human beings).

sentence.da: Der er kun en **person** i huset, og det er min far.
sentence.en: There is only one person in the house, and it is my father.

en pige.explanation: "En pige" means "a girl". It can also mean "a girlfriend" or "a young woman", but for a grown woman "en kvinde" (a woman) is safer. The matching word is "en dreng" (a boy).

sentence.da: Den lille **pige** har en rød kjole.
sentence.en: The little girl has a red dress.

en pille.explanation: "En pille" means "a pill" or "a tablet". You say "at tage en pille" (to take a pill). "Pillen" (the pill) can also mean the birth control pill.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i hovedet, så jeg tager en **pille**.
sentence.en: My head hurts, so I take a pill.

en pingvin.explanation: "En pingvin" means "a penguin". Danish spells the sound with "v" ("pingvin"), where English has "gu" ("penguin").

sentence.da: En **pingvin** er en fugl, der kan svømme, men ikke flyve.
sentence.en: A penguin is a bird that can swim but not fly.

en pizza.explanation: "En pizza" means "a pizza". To order one to take away, say "en pizza til at tage med" (a pizza to take with you).

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten, så jeg bestiller en **pizza** med ost.
sentence.en: I am hungry, so I order a pizza with cheese.

en plads.explanation: "En plads" means "a seat", "room" (space) or "a town square". On a train or in a cinema, "en plads" is your seat. "Er der plads?" means "Is there room?".

sentence.da: Bussen er fuld, så der er ikke **plads** til mig.
sentence.en: The bus is full, so there is no room for me.

en plan.explanation: "En plan" means "a plan". You can ask "Har du planer i weekenden?" (Do you have plans this weekend?). "At planlægge" means "to plan", and "en køreplan" means "a timetable".

sentence.da: Min **plan** er først at købe ind og så at lave mad.
sentence.en: My plan is first to shop and then to cook.

en plastikpose.explanation: "En plastikpose" means "a plastic bag", from "plastik" (plastic) and "en pose" (a bag). In shops you may hear "Vil du have en pose?" (Do you want a bag?).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger æblerne i en **plastikpose** og går hjem.
sentence.en: I put the apples in a plastic bag and go home.

en politistation.explanation: "En politistation" means "a police station", built from "politi" (police) and "station" (station). You say "på politistationen" (at the police station).

sentence.da: Politibetjenten arbejder på en **politistation**.
sentence.en: The police officer works at a police station.

en portion.explanation: "En portion" means "a portion" or "a serving", such as one person's share of food. In restaurants you may hear "en lille portion" (a small portion) or "en stor portion" (a large one). It is said por-ti-ON, with the stress on the last part.

sentence.da: Jeg er meget sulten, så jeg vil have en stor **portion** mad.
sentence.en: I am very hungry, so I want a big portion of food.

en pose.explanation: "En pose" means "a bag", a soft bag made of plastic or paper. A bag you carry, such as a handbag, is "en taske" (a bag, purse).

sentence.da: Jeg lagde æblerne i en **pose** af papir.
sentence.en: I put the apples in a paper bag.

en pris.explanation: "En pris" means "a price", what something costs. The same word also means a prize or award, so the situation tells you which: "en pris på tyve kroner" (a price of twenty crowns) is a price, while "at vinde en pris" (to win a prize) is an award.

sentence.da: Den her trøje har en lav **pris**, kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: This sweater has a low price, only twenty crowns.

en pude.explanation: "En pude" means "a pillow" and also a cushion, for example on a sofa. A bed pillow can be called "en hovedpude" (literally "a head pillow").

sentence.da: Jeg ligger i min seng med hovedet på en blød **pude**.
sentence.en: I lie in my bed with my head on a soft pillow.

en pung.explanation: "En pung" means "a wallet", a small one for coins and notes. "En tegnebog" (a wallet) means almost the same thing, but "pung" is the one you hear in everyday speech: "Jeg har glemt min pung" (I have forgotten my wallet).

sentence.da: Jeg har penge og et betalingskort i min **pung**.
sentence.en: I have money and a payment card in my wallet.

en pyjamas.explanation: "En pyjamas" means "a pair of pajamas". Danish treats it as one thing, so you say "en pyjamas" (literally "a pajamas") where English says "a pair of pajamas".

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **pyjamas** på og går i seng.
sentence.en: I put on my pajamas and go to bed.

en pære.explanation: "En pære" means "a pear" and also "a light bulb", so the situation tells you which one is meant: "en saftig pære" (a juicy pear) is fruit, while "en ny pære til lampen" (a new bulb for the lamp) is a light bulb.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en sød **pære** og et æble.
sentence.en: I eat a sweet pear and an apple.

en pølse.explanation: "En pølse" means "a sausage". A hot dog is "en hotdog" or "en pølse i brød" (a sausage in bread), and a street stand that sells them is "en pølsevogn" (a sausage wagon).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **pølse** med brød og sennep.
sentence.en: I eat a hot sausage with bread and mustard.

et par.explanation: "Et par" means "a pair" or "a couple", as in "et par sko" (a pair of shoes). It also means "a few": "et par dage" means "a couple of days". Two people in a relationship are also "et par" (a couple).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver her et **par** dage.
sentence.en: I will stay here for a couple of days.

et par jeans.explanation: "Et par jeans" means "a pair of jeans". You can also just say "jeans": "Jeg har jeans på" means "I am wearing jeans".

sentence.da: Mine bukser er gamle, så jeg køber **et par jeans**.
sentence.en: My pants are old, so I am buying a pair of jeans.

et pas.explanation: "Et pas" means "a passport", the document you show at the border. "Husk dit pas" means "Remember your passport". Do not mix it up with "at passe" (to fit, to look after), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Ved grænsen skal du vise dit **pas**.
sentence.en: At the border you must show your passport.

et plaster.explanation: "Et plaster" means "a band-aid", a small sticky bandage for a cut. "At sætte et plaster på" means "to put a band-aid on".

sentence.da: Sæt et **plaster** på såret.
sentence.en: Put a band-aid on the cut.

et postkontor.explanation: "Et postkontor" means "a post office", where you send letters and parcels. It is built from "post" (mail) and "kontor" (office). You may also hear "et posthus" (a post office), which means the same.

sentence.da: Jeg går til et **postkontor** for at sende en pakke og købe frimærker.
sentence.en: I am going to a post office to send a parcel and buy stamps.

et postkort.explanation: "Et postkort" means "a postcard", a card you send by mail. It is built from "post" (mail) and "kort" (card).

sentence.da: Fra ferien sender jeg et **postkort** med et frimærke til min mor.
sentence.en: From my holiday I send a postcard with a stamp to my mother.

et problem.explanation: "Et problem" means "a problem". "Det er ikke noget problem" means "It is no problem". "Hvad er problemet?" means "What is the problem?".

sentence.da: Bilen starter ikke, så vi har et **problem**.
sentence.en: The car will not start, so we have a problem.

et prøverum.explanation: "Et prøverum" means "a fitting room", the small room in a clothing shop where you try on clothes. It is built from "at prøve" (to try) and "et rum" (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg tager bukserne med ind i et **prøverum** for at prøve dem.
sentence.en: I take the pants into a fitting room to try them on.

forms.en: There is a deposit on the bottle

pant.explanation: "Pant" means "deposit": a small extra amount added to the price of a bottle or can, which you get back when you return the empty bottle.

sentence.da: Der er **pant** på flasken, så jeg får penge tilbage.
sentence.en: There is a deposit on the bottle, so I get money back.

papir.explanation: "Papir" means "paper", the material you write or print on. "Et stykke papir" (a piece of paper) is one sheet. "Papirer" can also mean "documents" (official papers).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver med en blyant på et stykke **papir**.
sentence.en: I write with a pencil on a piece of paper.

pas på.explanation: "Pas på" means "watch out" or "be careful". It can be a warning shouted in an emergency or a calm reminder, like "pas på, det er varmt" (careful, it is hot). It also means "look after": "pas på børnene" is "look after the children".

sentence.da: **Pas på**, gulvet er vådt!
sentence.en: Watch out, the floor is wet!

forms.da: Pas på dig selv i trafikken.
forms.en: Look after yourself in the traffic.

pas på dig selv.explanation: "Pas på dig selv" means "take care of yourself" and is a warm way to say goodbye. To several people, say "pas på jer selv" (take care of yourselves).

sentence.da: Farvel, og **pas på dig selv**!
sentence.en: Goodbye, and take care of yourself!

pasta.explanation: "Pasta" means "pasta", and it is spelled and said much like in English. You do not count it, so you say "Jeg laver pasta" (I am making pasta) with nothing in front of it.

sentence.da: Jeg koger **pasta** og laver en tomatsovs til.
sentence.en: I boil pasta and make a tomato sauce to go with it.

peber.explanation: "Peber" means "pepper", the spice you put on food. It is used without "a", as in "salt og peber" (salt and pepper). Do not mix it up with "peberfrugt" (bell pepper), which is a vegetable.

sentence.da: Jeg tilføjer lidt salt og **peber**.
sentence.en: I add a little salt and pepper.

penge.explanation: "Penge" means "money". It only comes in the "more than one" form, so there is no "a money". For one coin or one note, say "en mønt" (a coin) or "en seddel" (a banknote).

sentence.da: Billetten er dyr, og jeg har ikke mange **penge**.
sentence.en: The ticket is expensive, and I do not have much money.

perfekt.explanation: "Perfekt" means "perfect", just like in English. On its own it works as an exclamation: "Perfekt!" means "Great, that works!".

sentence.da: Alt er **perfekt**: solen skinner, og maden smager godt.
sentence.en: Everything is perfect: the sun is shining and the food tastes good.

pludselig.explanation: "Pludselig" means "suddenly" and also "sudden". "Pludselig kom han ind" means "Suddenly he came in". "Lige pludselig" is a bit stronger, like "all of a sudden".

sentence.da: Det var stille, men **pludselig** hørte jeg et højt brag.
sentence.en: It was quiet, but suddenly I heard a loud bang.

polen.explanation: "Polen" means "Poland". A person from there is "en polak" (a Pole) and the language is "polsk" (Polish).

sentence.da: Warszawa er hovedstaden i **Polen**, og man taler polsk der.
sentence.en: Warsaw is the capital of Poland, and people speak Polish there.

politi.explanation: "Politi" means "police". Danish treats it as one thing, so you say "politiet er her" (the police is here). One officer is "en politibetjent" (a police officer).

sentence.da: Der er kommet **politi** og ambulance, for der har været en ulykke.
sentence.en: Police and an ambulance have come, because there has been an accident.

polsk.explanation: "Polsk" means "Polish", for things from Poland and for the language. It is written with a small letter: "polsk", not "Polsk". A person is "en polak" (a Pole).

sentence.da: Min nabo kommer fra Polen og taler **polsk**.
sentence.en: My neighbour comes from Poland and speaks Polish.

pommes frites.explanation: "Pommes frites" means "French fries". Danes often shorten it to "pommes" (fries).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **pommes frites** og ketchup.
sentence.en: I would like fries and ketchup.

post.explanation: "Post" means "mail": the letters and parcels that arrive. It is also the word for the postal service. The person who delivers it is "postbudet" (the mail carrier), and the office is "postkontoret" (the post office).

sentence.da: Postbuddet kommer hver dag med **post** til os.
sentence.en: The mail carrier comes every day with mail for us.

præcis.explanation: "Præcis" means "exactly" or "precisely", and is used for time, amounts and details. On its own, "Præcis!" means "Exactly!" or "That's right!". For a rough amount, use "cirka" (approximately) instead.

sentence.da: Toget kommer **præcis** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The train comes exactly at eight o'clock.

på.explanation: "På" means "on", but also "at" or "in" in many fixed phrases: "på arbejde" (at work), "på ferie" (on holiday), "på dansk" (in Danish). Learn these as whole phrases. It is also used with islands and streets: "på Fyn" (on Funen), "på gaden" (on the street).

sentence.da: Telefonen ligger **på** bordet.
sentence.en: The phone is on the table.

på gensyn.explanation: "På gensyn" means "until we see each other again" and is a polite, slightly formal goodbye. With friends, "vi ses" (see you) is more usual.

sentence.da: Tak for besøget. **På gensyn!**
sentence.en: Thanks for the visit. See you again!

på tilbud.explanation: "På tilbud" means "on sale", with a lower price for a short time. It comes from "et tilbud" (an offer).

sentence.da: Kaffen er **på tilbud**, så den er billigere end normalt.
sentence.en: The coffee is on sale, so it is cheaper than usual.

forms.en: The bus is on its way.

på vej.explanation: "På vej" means "on the way" and is used for both coming and going. Say "jeg er på vej" when you are travelling toward a place, and add where to, like "på vej til arbejde" (on the way to work).

sentence.da: Jeg er **på vej** hjem og er der om ti minutter.
sentence.en: I am on my way home and will be there in ten minutes.

påske.explanation: "Påske" means "Easter". You use it without "a" or "the" in "til påske" (at Easter), but "i påsken" is how you say "during Easter". The greeting is "Glædelig påske!" (Happy Easter!).

sentence.da: Til **påske** maler børnene æg og får lidt chokolade.
sentence.en: At Easter the children paint eggs and get some chocolate.

pæn.explanation: "Pæn" means "nice-looking", "neat" or "tidy". It is used for people and things that look good in a simple way, for tidy rooms, and for good behaviour: "vær pæn" means "be well-behaved".

sentence.da: Du ser **pæn** ud i den nye kjole.
sentence.en: You look nice in the new dress.
